issues.title: Reproduce the flaky upgrade test before fixing it
issues.scope: test_real_upgrade_and_state_migration failed once and then passed on rerun with no code change. The previous backlog prescribed pinning the ledger sequence, but that fix was never tied to a reproduction, and the likelier cause is elsewhere: contractimport! reads the fixture wasm at compile time, and this project has already hit a Windows os error 32 file-in-use failure building that fixture. A pin at sequence 1000 is currently in the file — not the 100_000 the old issue specified — so the existing state matches neither the diagnosis nor the prescription. Reproduce first.
acceptance: Attempt reproduction deliberately: delete the fixture's target directory, run `cargo test` without rebuilding the fixture, and record what happens
Attempt reproduction with the ledger pin removed, across at least 20 runs, and record the pass rate
State which hypothesis the evidence supports — build ordering, ledger sequence, both, or neither — and say so plainly if it could not be reproduced at all
The ADR records the investigation and its conclusion, including a negative result if that is the outcome. A fix applied without a reproduction is explicitly called out as not acceptable here
nonGoals: Do not apply a fix in this issue. E05-02 does that, informed by this.

issues.title: Fix the upgrade test flake at its established root cause
issues.scope: Apply the fix that E05-01's evidence actually supports, rather than the one the old backlog guessed at.
acceptance: The change addresses the cause identified in ADR 0008 and the PR says which
If the ledger pin is retained, its value is justified rather than arbitrary, and a comment explains what it protects against
If the pin is not the fix, it is removed and the comment explaining its absence replaces it
`cargo test` run at least 10 consecutive times with no code change between runs; the PR states the count and pastes at least the first and last
The fixture is rebuilt from clean before the final run, so the tested path is the one a fresh contributor hits
nonGoals: No other test touched.

issues.title: Make the fixture build dependency explicit rather than tribal knowledge
issues.scope: cargo test silently fails or uses a stale binary if the v2 fixture has not been built, because contractimport! resolves its path at compile time. Today the only thing that communicates this is a comment in test.rs. A new contributor who runs cargo test first will hit a confusing error.
acceptance: Pick one mechanism and justify it: a build script that fails with a clear message when the fixture wasm is absent, or a test script that builds the fixture then runs cargo test
Running the chosen entry point from a clean checkout with no fixture target/ directory produces either a working run or an error message that names the exact command to fix it
README's test section uses this entry point
Demonstrate it: delete the fixture target/, run it, paste the output
nonGoals: Do not vendor the fixture wasm into the repo.

issues.title: Test the lock-period boundaries at both ends
issues.scope: The configured range is inclusive at both ends. Off-by-one at a boundary is the most likely defect in range validation and the easiest to miss, because a test using a mid-range value passes either way.
acceptance: Deposit with lock_ledgers exactly equal to min_lock_ledgers succeeds
Deposit with lock_ledgers exactly equal to max_lock_ledgers succeeds
Deposit one below min fails with InvalidLockPeriod
Deposit one above max fails with InvalidLockPeriod
The resulting unlock_ledger is asserted for the two successful cases, not just the absence of an error
nonGoals: Constructor and update_config validation are E05-05.

issues.title: Test constructor and update_config reject invalid bounds
issues.scope: Both entry points apply the same validation and both must reject the same inputs, or an admin can reach a state the constructor would have refused.
acceptance: Registering with min == 0 fails
Registering with max < min fails
Registering with min == max succeeds — a single fixed lock period is a legitimate configuration
update_config rejects the same two invalid cases and the stored bounds are unchanged after each rejection
The assertion style matches whatever E02-03 chose for constructor failures, and the PR notes that the two entry points fail in the same way
nonGoals: Authorization is E04-06.

issues.title: Test that pause blocks both deposit and withdraw
issues.scope: FR-5 is specific: pause halts new deposits and withdrawals, and never unlocks funds early. Both halves need pinning, and the second half is the one that matters for user trust.
acceptance: Deposit while paused fails with Error::Paused
Withdraw of a matured vault while paused fails with Error::Paused
After unpause, both succeed
A test asserts pause does not change any vault's unlock_ledger — pausing must never be a backdoor to early access, and must never lock funds permanently either
nonGoals: Authorization is E04-03.

issues.title: Test the remaining error variants each have a triggering test
issues.scope: NFR-2 requires every Error variant to be exercised by a test that actually triggers it. Several are covered by issues elsewhere in E03, E04 and E05; this issue closes whatever is left and proves the set is complete.
acceptance: AssetNotWhitelisted: deposit of a never-whitelisted asset fails with it
InsufficientBalance: withdraw of more than the vault holds fails with it, and the balance is unchanged afterwards
TimelockNotExpired: withdraw before unlock_ledger fails with it, including the exact boundary — withdrawing at sequence == unlock_ledger must succeed, one before must fail
VaultNotFound: get_vault and withdraw for a nonexistent vault id both fail with it
InvalidAmount: zero and negative on both deposit and withdraw
The PR contains a table mapping every Error variant to the test that triggers it, which is the NFR-2 evidence
nonGoals: NotInitialized is handled by E04-09, which may remove it.

issues.title: Assert every event's topic count stays within the ceiling
issues.scope: NFR-3 treats 4 topics as a hard ceiling. The SDK's type system does not enforce it, so nothing currently prevents someone adding a fifth #[topic]. There is also an unresolved question the project flagged and never answered: whether a bare #[contractevent] prepends an implicit name topic, which would change every event's real count. This test settles both.
acceptance: A test triggers every event type and reads env.events().all()
The actual topic count of each event is asserted, and the PR prints the observed topics per event type so the implicit-name-topic question is answered with evidence
No event exceeds 4 topics
DepositEvent and WithdrawEvent are confirmed to carry vault_id and amount as data rather than topics, per NFR-3's high-cardinality rule
The finding is recorded in docs/contract-interface.md, since the backend's decoders depend on it
nonGoals: Not changing any event's shape unless the count exceeds 4, in which case stop and open a separate issue.

issues.title: Assert event payload contents, not just that events fire
issues.scope: The backend reconstructs all user-facing state from these events, so a wrong field is a wrong dashboard with no other detection path. Asserting an event fired is not enough; the values have to be checked.
acceptance: DepositEvent carries the correct from, asset, vault_id and amount for a known deposit
WithdrawEvent carries the correct to, asset, vault_id and the amount withdrawn — not the remaining balance, which is the obvious way to get this wrong
A partial withdrawal's event amount is the withdrawn portion; assert this explicitly
Admin events carry the acting admin, and NewAdminEvent carries both old and new addresses
nonGoals: Backend decoding is E08.

issues.title: Test deposit and withdraw at i128 amount extremes
issues.scope: Balances are i128. The arithmetic in withdraw subtracts from a stored balance, and deposit stores a caller-supplied amount directly. Large values are cheap to test and the failure mode is a corrupted balance.
acceptance: A deposit of i128::MAX either succeeds with the exact stored amount or fails cleanly; assert which and state it in the PR
A second deposit that would overflow a summed balance is examined — note that each deposit creates a separate vault, so confirm whether balances are ever summed on-chain and say so
Withdrawing the full i128 balance leaves exactly zero, with no wraparound
The token mint used in the test is large enough that the token contract is not the limiting factor; if it is, say so rather than reporting a false pass
nonGoals: No fuzzing.

issues.title: Test withdrawal at the exact unlock ledger boundary
issues.scope: The check is `sequence < unlock_ledger` returns TimelockNotExpired, so withdrawal at exactly unlock_ledger is allowed. That is a deliberate boundary choice and should be pinned, because flipping it to <= is a one-character change that no mid-range test would catch.
acceptance: Withdrawal at sequence == unlock_ledger - 1 fails with TimelockNotExpired
Withdrawal at sequence == unlock_ledger succeeds
The test name states the boundary, and a comment records that inclusive-at-unlock is the intended semantics
The same boundary is reflected in docs/contract-interface.md so the frontend does not show a vault as locked when the contract would allow the withdrawal
nonGoals: No change to the comparison.

issues.title: Organise the test module into labelled sections
issues.scope: test.rs will hold roughly forty tests once this milestone lands, added by many contributors across many PRs. Without structure, finding whether a case is already covered becomes guesswork and duplicates appear.
acceptance: Tests are grouped into clearly commented sections: setup helpers, vault operations, lock periods, authorization, storage lifecycle, events, upgrade
No test is renamed or changed in behaviour — this is organisation only, and the PR confirms the test count is identical before and after
`cargo test` green with the same number of tests as before
nonGoals: No splitting into multiple files unless the module exceeds what one file can carry readably; if it does, raise it rather than deciding unilaterally.

issues.title: Measure and record contract test coverage
issues.scope: NFR-2 is stated in terms of error variants, which is a good floor but says nothing about branch coverage. Measure once so the gaps are visible and future claims about coverage are grounded.
acceptance: A coverage tool is run against the contract crate; the tool and version are named and the command recorded
The report is summarised per source file with the real numbers
Every uncovered branch is listed with a one-line judgement: acceptable, or needs an issue — and if it needs one, the issue is opened
The doc states the date and the commit it describes
nonGoals: No coverage gate in CI yet; establish the baseline first.

issues.title: Test that deposit transfers tokens before recording the vault
issues.scope: deposit calls the token's transfer first and writes vault state after. If the transfer fails the whole transaction reverts, so no vault should exist. Assert that, because a vault recorded without the corresponding tokens actually arriving is the worst failure this contract could have.
acceptance: A deposit by a user with insufficient token balance fails
After that failure get_user_vault_count is unchanged and no vault entry exists
The vault contract's token balance is unchanged
A successful deposit in the same test confirms the setup is otherwise sound
nonGoals: Not testing malicious token contracts; that trust boundary is documented in E04-11.

issues.title: Test that withdraw records state before transferring out
issues.scope: The mirror of E05-14. withdraw writes the decremented balance before calling transfer, which is the correct ordering. Pin it so a future refactor that reorders them is caught.
acceptance: A successful withdrawal leaves the stored balance and the token balances mutually consistent
A withdrawal that fails the timelock check moves no tokens and changes no balance
A withdrawal that fails the insufficient-balance check moves no tokens and changes no balance
A comment records that state-before-transfer is deliberate ordering, not incidental
nonGoals: No reordering of the implementation.

issues.title: Test a full deposit-to-empty lifecycle in one scenario
issues.scope: Unit tests cover each step in isolation. One end-to-end scenario through the contract catches interaction bugs the isolated tests cannot — for example a counter that is correct after one deposit and wrong after three.
acceptance: One user makes three deposits across two assets with different lock periods
Locks mature at different ledgers and each vault is withdrawn, some partially first
Balances and vault ids are asserted at every step, not only at the end
The final state matches what E03-02 decided for zero-balance vaults
Token balances reconcile exactly: what left the user equals what the vault holds, at every step
nonGoals: Not a replacement for the unit tests.

issues.title: Test that the upgrade preserves vault balances across many entries
issues.scope: The existing upgrade test migrates a single vault. The real risk in an upgrade is a partial or inconsistent migration across many entries, which one entry cannot reveal.
acceptance: Several vaults across multiple users and assets are created before the upgrade
After the upgrade every one is readable through the new binary with its exact pre-upgrade balance and unlock_ledger
UserVaultCount is intact for each user
The contract address is unchanged throughout, and version() confirms the bytecode actually swapped
nonGoals: Not a live testnet upgrade; that is E06-12.

issues.title: Test that admin state survives an upgrade
issues.scope: Vault balances are the obvious thing to check across an upgrade. Admin, pause state and config live in instance storage and are equally load-bearing — an upgrade that silently reset the admin would hand the contract to nobody, or to whoever the new binary's constructor names.
acceptance: Admin address is identical before and after the upgrade
Pause state survives: pause, upgrade, and assert still paused
Whitelist entries survive
The PR notes explicitly whether the new binary's constructor runs on upgrade — it must not, and this test is the evidence
nonGoals: Not testing a migration that deliberately changes admin.

issues.title: Document how to run the contract test suite from a clean checkout
issues.scope: The fixture build ordering, the toolchain version requirement and the wasm target are all things a new contributor will hit in their first ten minutes. Write the path that works.
acceptance: Documents the required toolchain: Rust 1.85 or later because soroban-sdk 28's dependency tree needs edition2024, and the wasm32v1-none target
Gives the exact PowerShell command sequence from clean checkout to green suite
Explains the fixture build ordering and what the failure looks like if it is skipped
Every command was actually run on a clean checkout and the output is in the PR
Linked from README and CONTRIBUTING
nonGoals: Not documenting backend or frontend testing; those come with their own epics.

issues.title: Add the contract test count and coverage summary to CI output
issues.scope: CI currently passes or fails. Surfacing the test count makes a silently-skipped or deleted test visible in review, which is the realistic way coverage regresses on a project with many contributors.
acceptance: The workflow prints the test count in its summary
The job fails if the suite reports zero tests run, which would otherwise look like success
The run is green on the introducing PR and the count matches a local run
nonGoals: No coverage threshold gate yet.

issues.title: Run the full suite repeatedly to check for remaining nondeterminism
issues.scope: One test in this suite has already been observed to flake. With roughly forty tests, several of them ledger- and TTL-sensitive, a single green run is weak evidence. Check the whole suite the way the upgrade test should have been checked.
acceptance: The full suite is run at least 25 consecutive times with no code change; the PR states the exact count and the pass rate
Any test that fails even once is reported with its output and gets its own issue — it is not retried until green
If all runs pass, that is recorded in docs/testing.md with the date and commit
Tests are also run single-threaded at least once to check for inter-test interference
nonGoals: Not fixing a flake found here; open an issue for it so the investigation gets its own scope.

issues.title: Assert the contract takes no fee on any path
issues.scope: FR-6 states there are no protocol fees in v1. That is currently true only because nobody wrote any, which is not the same as being enforced. A negative requirement with no test is exactly the kind of thing that erodes quietly — someone adds a small skim during a later feature and no test objects. Pin it now while it is trivially true.
acceptance: A test deposits a known amount and asserts the vault's recorded balance equals it exactly, with nothing withheld
A test withdraws the full balance and asserts the tokens received equal the amount deposited exactly
Token balances are reconciled across the whole round trip: what left the user's account equals what returned to it, and the vault contract holds zero afterwards
The test name states the invariant, and a comment records that FR-6 makes this a deliberate guarantee rather than an incidental property
The same reconciliation is asserted for a partial withdrawal, since a per-withdrawal fee would be easiest to hide there
nonGoals: Not designing a fee mechanism for a future version.

issues.title: Freeze the contract interface and record the milestone baseline
issues.scope: Backend and frontend work builds against this interface, and the whole point of finishing the contract milestone first is that off-chain work is not chasing a moving target. Record the frozen state so any later change is a visible, deliberate decision.
acceptance: contract-interface.md matches the built wasm exactly: exported functions, argument types, error codes and event shapes
The wasm hash and byte size are recorded alongside the commit
The ADR states that changes after this point require an issue explaining the impact on backend and frontend consumers
`cargo test` and `stellar contract build` output both pasted as the baseline evidence
nonGoals: Not preventing future change; making it deliberate.
